# Story Bank Material — Swoveralls, DudeRobe, DeFi Snacks

Compiled 2026-11-16 from published public sources only. Every item cites its source with URL and date. Quotes are exact. Nothing here is invented. Anything unverified is in each brand's Gaps section, not filled in.

Two corrections to note before use:
- DudeRobe is a SEPARATE company from DUDE Products / Dude Wipes (different founders, different city). Do not use Dude Wipes' story as DudeRobe material.
- Swoveralls founder is Kyle Bergman (not "Berman", as several recap sites spell it).

---


Brand: Swoveralls (swoveralls.com, Instagram @swoveralls_)
Parent company: The Great Fantastic, LLC
Compiled: 2026-11-16, from published public sources only.
Rule followed: every item below cites its source with URL and date. Quotes are exact as published. Anything unverified is in Gaps, not filled in.

Note on the founder's name: the correct spelling is **Kyle Bergman**. Several Shark Tank recap sites spell it "Berman" — that is their error, not the name.

## Origin / founder

**Founder:** Kyle Bergman, Founder & Chief Swoverall Officer of The Great Fantastic.
**Background (verified):** Drexel University, bachelor's in Psychology, 2012; played on the men's lacrosse team. First entrepreneurial venture was a club lacrosse programme and tournament run with a friend during his first Drexel co-op; later co-ops with a fashion photography company and a small tomato sauce company. His mother suggested retail; he joined the Bloomingdale's Executive Training programme and worked there 4 years (assistant buyer, luggage; senior assistant, women's fragrances; associate merchandise planner, jewelry). Joined Birchbox in May 2016 as Men's Grooming Buyer (2 years). Began a part-time MBA at NYU Stern while at Birchbox. Also a member of the Israel Men's National Lacrosse team, an Orangetheory Fitness trainer, and played on three world-championship teams.
- Source: https://www.thetriangle.org/article/drexel-grad-kyle-bergmans-swoveralls-on-shark-tank (Drexel Triangle, 2019-05-03); https://www.the360mag.com/on-shark-tank-swoveralls-worlds-comfiest-apparel/ (360 Magazine, 2019-05-21)

**The idea (founder's own words):** "At first, I was really just trying to solve a personal problem - Sweatpant overalls didn't exist, and I wanted a pair. I've always loved overalls for reasons I can't really explain."
- Source: https://www.starterstory.com/stories/sweatpants-overalls-how-i-turned-a-silly-idea-into-a-viral-brand (Starter Story, founder interview, published 2019; updated 2025-04-10)

**The trigger:** early 2016, a friend sent him a BuzzFeed article about novelty sweatpant overalls that looked like denim. The article showed only women's versions; he wanted a pair for himself. No normal sweatpant overalls existed online or in stores. He found a factory drawing of men's sweatpant overalls on Alibaba (minimum order 300 units), negotiated a single sample, and received it.
- Source: Starter Story interview above; https://sidehustleschool.com/episode/3042/ (Side Hustle School, episode 3042, 2025-04-30)

**The demand check:** in March 2017 he used Google's Keyword Planner and found 100–1,000 people a month searching for "sweatpant overalls". (A later brand film rounds this to "about 500 people per month".)
- Source: Starter Story interview above; https://www.instagram.com/reel/DaVwb0dvCRT/ (brand film, @swoveralls_, posted 2026-07-03)

**The company name:** The Great Fantastic, LLC, incorporated March 2017. "Taking a trip into the great fantastic is something my Mom would say when referring to risk-taking and adventuring into the unknown."
- Source: Starter Story interview above; https://swoveralls.com/pages/about

**Funding the first order:** he had taken out more student loan money than needed for his first MBA term and received a ~$10,000 disbursement. "I decided to use this money to kickstart my sweatpant overalls project, and used most of it to pay for my first order from overseas." He sent $10,000 to a supplier in China he had never met in person, only spoken to through Alibaba messaging. First order: 500 pairs (250 grey, 250 navy). No patents ("patenting apparel designs is like the wild west"); he did trademark the term "Swoveralls".
- Source: Starter Story interview above

**Mission (brand's own words):** "Our mission is to create the world's comfiest apparel using sustainable resources and ethical manufacturing processes." The brand's tagline, used in the 2026 brand film: "Free the Waistband" — "to make people more comfortable both literally and figuratively."
- Source: https://swoveralls.com/pages/about; https://www.the360mag.com/on-shark-tank-swoveralls-worlds-comfiest-apparel/ (2019-05-21); Instagram brand film 2026-07-03 (link above)

**Product, as the brand describes it:** sweatpants + overalls. Six pockets (including a hidden zip pocket in the bib), adjustable straps with metal buckles, jogger cuffs, zipper fly, no waistband. French terry, cotton-rich with a touch of stretch; GOTS-certified organic cotton. Gender neutral, sizes XXS–4XL (some styles to 5XL). Made in Los Angeles. Retail $95 at Shark Tank time (2019).
- Source: https://swoveralls.com/pages/meet-swoveralls; https://swoveralls.com/pages/about; 360 Magazine 2019-05-21

**Giveback:** proud partner/member of 1% for the Planet, Urban Pathways, and the Israel Lacrosse Association. A percentage of net profits from the Swoveralls 2.0 crowdfunding was donated to Urban Pathways and the Israel Lacrosse Association.
- Source: 360 Magazine 2019-05-21; https://www.prweb.com/releases/Sweatpant_overalls_Hybrid_Swoveralls_2_0_Nears_the_End_of_its_Successful_Kickstarter_Campaign/prweb15940523.htm (PRWeb, 2018-07-02)

**Founder today (side ventures):** partner and COO at Pinkberg (marketing strategy company) since 2023; co-founder and coach of Keep The Pace (exercise programmes) since 2021. In March 2020 he started a separate business, Sweat from Home, with two co-founders. The brand film (July 2026) shows his twin toddlers Max and Bernie.
- Source: https://www.women.com/1572934/what-went-down-swoveralls-after-shark-tank/ (updated 2025-01-31); https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-we-increased-our-sales-155-last-year (Starter Story follow-up, 2021-05-26); Instagram brand film 2026-07-03

## Press & interviews

**First press ever:** the first article anyone wrote about Swoveralls was on Fatherly; another early one came via his Birchbox job on Business Insider. (Dates not stated in the source; the Fatherly/Business Insider article URLs were not verified — see Gaps.)
- Source: Starter Story interview (founder's own account)

**Breakthrough feature:** a connection from his lacrosse network got Swoveralls featured in Thrillist; the article was then picked up by local news media and blogs worldwide. (The Thrillist article itself — date and URL — was not found; see Gaps.)
- Source: Side Hustle School episode 3042 (2025-04-30)

**Bustle, 2019-04-25:** "Swoveralls Combine Overalls & Sweatpants — What More Do You Need?" Quotes Bergman: "Our mission is to create the world's comfiest apparel using sustainable resources and ethical manufacturing processes. As an athlete, I recognize comfort is a universal concept that everyone understands and experiences, and Swoveralls make that concept accessible, inclusive, and fun." Notes the product was $95, in three colours (black, grey, navy), and stocked at The Phluid Project, "the world's first gender-free store".
- Source: https://www.bustle.com/p/swoveralls-combine-overalls-sweatpants-what-more-do-you-need-17199481

**Washington Square News (NYU), 2019-04-24:** "Stern Student Pitches Sweatpants-Overalls Company to the Sharks." Reports the pitch ($150,000 for 15% equity; all five sharks declined), the company founded March 2017, and that Bergman pitched again to Mark Cuban in January at a "Stern Tank" event, handing Cuban a pair of custom Swoveralls.
- Source: https://nyunews.com/news/2019/04/24/stern-student-pitches-swoveralls-to-shark-tank/

**Drexel Triangle, 2019-05-03:** "Drexel grad Kyle Bergman's 'Swoveralls' on Shark Tank." "The night that [the episode] aired, I had about 13,000 people visit my website, and in the week or so since it aired, I have had over 60,000 people visit my website." Backorder of six to eight weeks for the original colours (black, dark grey, navy). Plans to offer monthly limited-edition colours and designs crowd-sourced from customers.
- Source: https://www.thetriangle.org/article/drexel-grad-kyle-bergmans-swoveralls-on-shark-tank

**NYU Stern news, 2019-04-21:** "Swoveralls, founded by MBA student Kyle Bergman, is featured on ABC's 'Shark Tank'." Quotes the pitch: "Made from sustainably sourced organic cotton right here in the USA, Swoveralls possess the functionality of overalls while also providing extreme comfort."
- Source: https://www.stern.nyu.edu/experience-stern/news-events/swoveralls-founded-mba-student-kyle-bergman-featured-abc-s-shark-tank

**Starter Story founder interview, 2019 (updated 2025-04-10):** "How I Turned A Silly Idea Into A $1M+ Brand." First-person account of the origin, Alibaba, Keyword Planner, Amazon FBA, incorporation, crowdfunding, and the viral Facebook video (9M+ views, made with Margle Media, posted to the "22 words" page).
- Source: https://www.starterstory.com/stories/sweatpants-overalls-how-i-turned-a-silly-idea-into-a-viral-brand

**Starter Story follow-up, 2021-05-26:** "How We Increased Our Sales 155% Last Year." "When we first appeared on Starter Story back in 2019 we were averaging about $17k/month in revenue, and have since grown to just about $60k/month so far in 2021!" "From a sales standpoint, we've doubled our annual sales each year, and are already 155% above last year! We're still self-funded." Returning customer rate "about 30%". The Comfy Lab described (see Milestones). The Shark Tank episode "re-aired over 10x".
- Source: https://www.starterstory.com/stories/how-we-increased-our-sales-155-last-year

**360 Magazine press release, 2019-05-21:** "On Shark Tank, 'SWOVERALLS' World's Comfiest Apparel." Headline claims a "1,500% Sales Spike". "Since the show, we have had a 1,500% sales spike in Swoveralls, and are only taking preorders now as we rush to restock inventory." Also: "Since the show, at the time of this release, The Great Fantastic has now sold over $320,000 in Swoveralls, with more than 3,000 happy and comfy customers!"
- Source: https://www.the360mag.com/on-shark-tank-swoveralls-worlds-comfiest-apparel/

**Side Hustle School, episode 3042, 2025-04-30:** "Fashion Buyer Creates Quirky Comfort Craze." Update/remix of the original episode 394. "He generated over $65,000 in sales in his first year, resulting in $24,000 in profit." Launch mailing list of 700 contacts compiled by hand; product models from his lacrosse network; branding "inspired by Chubby Swim Shorts".
- Source: https://sidehustleschool.com/episode/3042/

**Brand press page (swoveralls.com/pages/press) — outlets that have featured Swoveralls, as listed by the brand (dates not shown on the page):**
- Cool Material, "The 8 Best Men's Overalls, From Workwear Staples To High Style": "Swoveralls are a comfortable alternative to heavier denim or canvas material for all-day comfort, whether lounging at home or out on the town."
- Cool Material, "What We're Buying: Corduroy Swoveralls": "I opted to get some corduroy Swoveralls last week and I've worn them three times already this week (for reference, it's only Tuesday when I'm writing this)."
- Finders & Keep, "Swoveralls Review: The Best Work-From-Home Clothes Ever?": "My two favorite things about Swoveralls are their convenience and their versatility."

- Well+Good, "Cozy Gifts for the People in Your Life Who Love a Night (or All the Nights) In": "Made from a soft (and GOTS-certified) cotton material that's as comfortable as it is durable (and totally washer and dryer-friendly), these ultra-cozy overalls are perfect for all-day lounging, running errands, walking the dog, and other leisure activities. If self-care was an outfit, it'd be this."

**Shark Tank (ABC), Season 10 Episode 20, aired 21 April 2019:** Bergman asked $150,000 for 15% equity. No deal — all five sharks passed (Mark Cuban, Barbara Corcoran, Kevin O'Leary, Lori Greiner, Daymond John). Unit cost $33 to make in the US, retail $95. Sales of over $230,000 since launching in September (2017), through Amazon and direct-to-consumer. About $100,000 lost the previous year to inventory problems. Sharks' concerns: too many SKUs/colours, niche appeal, inventory risk. The pitch was filmed September 2018; Bergman was introduced to a casting producer in July 2018 through a Birchbox connection. He initially turned down the opportunity, feeling the company was not ready.
- Source: https://sharktankrecap.com/swoveralls-update-shark-tank-season-10/ (published 2025-06-14, updated 2026-01-07); https://www.thetriangle.org/article/drexel-grad-kyle-bergmans-swoveralls-on-shark-tank (2019-05-03); https://www.women.com/1572934/what-went-down-swoveralls-after-shark-tank/ (updated 2025-01-31)

## Milestones

- **Early 2016** — BuzzFeed article sparks the idea; friend sends it to Bergman while he is a merchandise planner at Bloomingdale's. (Starter Story)
- **March 2017** — The Great Fantastic, LLC incorporated. Google Keyword Planner shows 100–1,000 monthly searches for "sweatpant overalls". (Starter Story)
- **September 2017** — first sales launch (Amazon + direct-to-consumer). "I sold my first pair about 18 months ago" (Starter Story, April 2019) points to ~Oct 2017; the Shark Tank pitch says "launched in September". Exact day not published.
- **First year** — "a little over $65k in sales between Amazon and my own site" (Starter Story, founder). Side Hustle School: "over $65,000 in sales in his first year, resulting in $24,000 in profit." (Note: Washington Square News says "$230,000 in the first year" — that conflicts; see Gaps. The $230,000 figure is consistently reported as total sales by pitch time, April 2019.)
- **2017–2018** — first press: Fatherly, then Business Insider (Starter Story). Thrillist feature via a lacrosse-network connection; picked up by local news and blogs worldwide (Side Hustle School).
- **June–July 2018** — Swoveralls 2.0 crowdfunding: Kickstarter raised ~$75,000 (goal $10,000, beaten "in mere hours" / within the first 24 hours), Indiegogo ~$33,000, ~$108,000 total. 600+ backers. Production moved from overseas to Los Angeles. A Facebook video made with Margle Media went viral (9M+ views) via the "22 words" page. PRWeb release 2018-07-02 notes attention from The Today Show and UNILAD.
  - Source: Starter Story; https://www.prweb.com/releases/Sweatpant_overalls_Hybrid_Swoveralls_2_0_Nears_the_End_of_its_Successful_Kickstarter_Campaign/prweb15940523.htm (2018-07-02); Shark Tank Recap
- **July 2018** — introduced to a Shark Tank casting producer through a Birchbox connection. (Triangle)
- **September 2018** — flew to California to film Shark Tank. (Triangle)
- **21 April 2019** — Shark Tank Season 10 Episode 20 airs on ABC. Ask $150,000 for 15%; no deal. ~13,000 website visits the night it aired; 60,000+ in the week after. 1,500% sales spike reported (360 Mag, 2019-05-21). Backorder 6–8 weeks. Total sold passes $320,000 with 3,000+ customers by May 2019 (360 Mag).
- **Late 2019** — inventory issues worked out; The Comfy Lab launched on the website (micro-crowdfunding: customers pre-order limited-edition designs at 20% off; small batches, less waste). Swovie Shorts and Kids Swoveralls introduced.
  - Source: https://www.sharktankblog.com/business/swoveralls/; Starter Story follow-up 2021-05-26
- **2020** — pandemic: brand released masks; China factory shut Jan–Mar 2020, LA production kept working, then reversed. Two manufacturing facilities kept production going.
  - Source: Shark Tank Recap; Starter Story follow-up 2021-05-26
- **2021** — revenue ~$60k/month (from ~$17k/month in 2019); annual sales doubled each year; 155% above the prior year; ~30% returning customer rate; still self-funded, selling only via own website and Amazon. New products: Swovie Shorts (winner), Kids Swoveralls, limited editions (tie-dye, Light Heather Grey, Pink for a breast cancer awareness foundation, NASA collaboration). Dog Swoveralls test run did not do well.
  - Source: Starter Story follow-up 2021-05-26
- **24 August 2023** — Comfyalls (heavier cold-weather version) launched for pre-order, 30% off.
  - Source: https://milled.com/swoveralls/early-access-introducing-comfyalls-FKxTGuzCsdvR77F0 (email sent 2023-08-24)
- **Late 2023** — roughly $4 million in annual revenue; website traffic peaked around 1.2 million monthly visits. (Third-party estimate from Shark Tank Recap/Blog — not founder-confirmed; see Gaps.)
  - Source: https://sharktankrecap.com/swoveralls-update-shark-tank-season-10/ (2025-06-14); https://www.sharktankblog.com/business/swoveralls/
- **2025** — Customer Design Contest: Elizabeth Brown's Otter print wins. Brand still owner-operated; Kyle still owns the business. Products made in Los Angeles using sustainable materials.
  - Source: https://swoveralls.com/products/swoveralls-otter-romp; Shark Tank Recap
- **19 February 2026** — Yo Gabba Gabba! licensing announcement (License Global): "Swoveralls will introduce 'Yo Gabba Gabba!'-themed apparel, both set to hit retail this summer." Products (Kammy Kubes and GooBle Search prints, adults $89.99–$120, kids $43.99) listed on the official Yo Gabba Gabba store by August 2026; Yo Gabba Gabba's Facebook post promoting the collaboration 2026-08-25.
  - Source: https://www.licenseglobal.com/streaming-tv/-yo-gabba-gabba-introduces-licensing-rollout-following-new-season (2026-02-19); https://www.yogabbagabba.com/collections/all?page=2; https://swoveralls.com/products/swoveralls-kammy-kubes
- **3 July 2026** — brand film on Instagram (@swoveralls_): founder Kyle narrates the journey from idea to prototype to first order to the Shark Tank stage; mission stated as "Free the Waistband". Features twin toddlers Max and Bernie.
  - Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DaVwb0dvCRT/
- **2026 (current range)** — product line: Swoveralls (original), Swovie Shorts, Kids Swoveralls, Comfyalls, limited-edition prints and collaborations (Yo Gabba Gabba!, NASA, breast cancer awareness foundation). Sold via swoveralls.com and Amazon. "Free the Waistband: 25% off everything" Black Friday sale (code BF-25, runs through 1 Dec).
  - Source: https://swoveralls.com/pages/black-friday-sale; Starter Story follow-up 2021-05-26

**No outside capital:** "Kyle never raised any outside capital. He used Kickfurther to meet high demand during key seasons and kept full ownership." (Third-party report — see Gaps.)
- Source: Shark Tank Recap

## Gaps / not found

- **Thrillist article:** the breakthrough feature is confirmed by Side Hustle School, but the Thrillist article itself (date, URL, headline) was not found. Do not cite a Thrillist date or link until verified.
- **Fatherly / Business Insider first articles:** confirmed only by the founder's account in Starter Story; the article URLs and dates were not verified.
- **Reddit customer stories:** a site:reddit.com search for Swoveralls returned no results. No Reddit threads were found to quote. (This does not prove none exist — only that none were found via search.)
- **Awards:** no awards found in any source searched. Do not claim any.
- **Funding / valuation beyond crowdfunding:** no outside investment found. The "$4 million annual revenue (late 2023)" and "$5 million net worth (2025)" figures come from third-party Shark Tank recap sites (Shark Tank Recap, Shark Tank Blog, Geeks Around Globe), not from the founder or the brand — treat as estimates, not facts.
- **Conflicting figures — flag before using:**
  - First-year sales: Starter Story (founder) and Side Hustle School say ~$65,000; Washington Square News (2019-04-24) says "over $230,000 in the first year". The $230,000 figure is consistently reported elsewhere as total sales by the April 2019 pitch. Use $65k for year one and $230k for sales-to-pitch.
  - Sample price: Starter Story says the single sample was "about $80"; Side Hustle School says quoted $150, negotiated down to $111. Do not use a sample price without noting the conflict.
  - Kickstarter totals: $75,000 (Kickstarter) + $33,000 (Indiegogo) = ~$108,000 per the founder; some recap sites report $108,396 (Indiegogo alone) or add ~$75,000 from Backer Club. Use the founder's figures.
- **Giveback org list on the About page:** the page text ("We are proud supporters and members of the following organizations:") did not render the list in the crawl. The three orgs named here (1% for the Planet, Urban Pathways, Israel Lacrosse Association) come from the 360 Magazine release — verify against the live About page before using the list as complete.
- **Exact first-sale date:** only "September 2017" (pitch) / "~18 months before April 2019" (Starter Story). No exact day published.
- **Founder interviews beyond the above:** no podcast appearances other than Side Hustle School (episodes 394 and 3042) were found. No TV appearances beyond Shark Tank were found.
- **Customer interviews beyond Elizabeth and Lance:** the brand's Comfy Interviews page and Customer of the Month pages exist but the full index of entries was not enumerated. More customer stories may exist on swoveralls.com/pages/comfyinterviews and the customer-of-the-month pages.

Researched 2026-11-16. Every item below comes from a published public source, cited with URL and date. Quotes are exact. Nothing here is invented. Items I could not verify are in **Gaps** at the end, not filled in.

**Headline:** DudeRobe is a men's hooded bathrobe/loungewear brand founded by Howie Busch (Long Island, New York). Kickstarter June 2017 ($67,498), Shark Tank Season 9, Episode 16 (aired 14 Jan 2018, no deal). It is a **separate company from DUDE Products / Dude Wipes** — different founders, different city, different product. See "DUDE Wipes connection" below.

## Origin / founder

**Founder:** Howie Busch, from Long Island, New York. Former attorney and former sports agent (Boardroom calls him a "former NFL agent"); inventor before DudeRobe — he created the On-Hand Pillow and the World's Smallest Travel Pillow, sold in airports worldwide. Former coach for inventRight. (Sources: Gazette Review, 4 Aug 2018; Boardroom, 15 Dec 2021; Jon Dwoskin interview, 16 Apr 2021; inventRight TV podcast.)

**The idea (founder's own account, brand's Our Story page):**
> "It was 2016. I'm in the shower… Then I turned around and saw my hoodie hanging on the hook next to my towel. That was it. What if a robe looked and felt like a hoodie, but actually dried you off?"
> — duderobe.com, Our Story page (undated, live Nov 2026)

He was never a "robe guy" but noticed his wife wore her robe every day and looked comfortable. He drove to Walmart, bought a stack of towels, and took them to his tailor José: *"José, can you make a hoodie out of these towels?"* One week later he had a prototype — hooded robe, tapered sleeves, permanently attached belt. (Same source.)

**Earlier telling (Gazette Review, 4 Aug 2018):** Busch saw his wife's bathrobe hanging next to a hoodie on a hook, drove to Walmart, bought six towels, and worked with his tailor on several prototypes over the next week (robe, sweatshirt, shorts).

**Work began 2015:** PRWeb launch release (19 Jun 2017) says "The team has been working hard since 2015… they have developed samples and is in negotiations with manufacturers."

**The product:** a hooded bathrobe that is sweatshirt material outside, terry towel inside — plus matching shorts, pants, hoodies. Features the brand stresses: permanently attached ("Never-Lost") belt, tapered/cuffed sleeves, deep pockets, hidden stash pocket. Current list price $128 (checked 1 Nov 2026, Yawnder); often sold at $89.60 (30% off) on duderobe.com.

**Founder quotes (PRWeb, 19 Jun 2017):**
> "We re-designed and re-engineered the robe into something today's guys will actually want to wear — something that's absorbent and also looks cool… You can wear it for lounging, but also when you walk the dog or get your morning coffee."
> "There are no good options for men's robes on the market today. The only alternative is the boring and oversized unisex robe."

**Under Armour connection (founder's claim on Shark Tank, per Gazette Review):** Busch says he was involved in the beginnings of Under Armour, negotiating contracts from his first year of law school, and declined equity at the time. This is his own account as reported; treat as founder-claimed, not independently verified.

### DUDE Wipes connection — VERIFIED: none

DudeRobe and DUDE Products (Dude Wipes) are **separate companies with no shared founders**:
- DudeRobe: Howie Busch, Long Island NY, founded 2017, Kickstarter.
- Dude Wipes: Sean Riley, Ryan Meegan, Jeff Klimkowski and Brian Wilkin, Chicago, founded 2011/2012, Shark Tank Season 7 (2015), $300,000 from Mark Cuban for 25%.
- No source other than one low-quality page claims any link. That page (sharktanksuccess.com, "DUDE Products Update") states "The company also branched out into clothing. They created the DudeRobe" — this contradicts the Kickstarter page (creator: Howie Busch), the PRWeb release, Inc., Boardroom, and all Shark Tank coverage. Treat it as an error. DUDE Products' own product range is wipes-led; no robe product of theirs was found.
- The shared "Dude" naming and the shared Shark Tank history are the only links, and both are coincidence, not corporate connection. Do **not** use Dude Wipes' story (Chicago apartment, Mark Cuban deal, $300M valuation) as DudeRobe material.

**1. PRWeb — launch press release, 19 Jun 2017**
"DudeRobe™ Introduces a Fashion Friendly Robe Designed Specifically for Today's Man." Reports "raised over $45K on Kickstarter and fully funded in just two days." Includes the Busch quotes above.

**2. Inc. — 27 Jun 2017, by Stephen Key**
"How Crowdfunding Will Make You a Better Entrepreneur." Interview with Busch during the campaign: "With three days left to go… he's raised nearly $57,000 for DudeRobe… Within just two days of going live, Busch met his goal of raising $25,000 on Kickstarter… Three weeks later, he had more than doubled his stated goal. But to truly establish proof of demand and secure a licensing deal, he hopes to raise at least $75,000."
https://www.inc.com/stephen-key/how-crowdfunding-will-make-you-a-better-entrepreneur.html

**3. Mic.com — 3 Jul 2017**
"The DudeRobe is here to prove, once and for all, that masculinity is so very fragile." Notes the Kickstarter video's line "Bathrobes are too girly" and that the campaign "raised more than $60,000, with funding wrapping on Friday" against a $25,000 goal. Creator described as "former sports agent Howie Busch."
https://www.mic.com/articles/181343/the-duderobe-is-here-to-prove-once-and-for-all-that-masculinity-is-so-very-fragile

**4. inventRight TV podcast — "The Impact of Appearing on Shark Tank" (Howie Busch interview)**
Busch: "I have never been a robe guy, but envied how comfortable his wife was when she got out of the shower… Towels were good. So were hoodies. Why not combine a towel with a hoodie?" Also: a Shark Tank producer contacted him one week into the Kickstarter. (Listen Notes page; episode date not stated on the page I read.)
https://www.listennotes.com/fr/podcasts/inventrighttv/the-impact-of-appearing-on-1DhSXR5Eis7/

**5. inventRight TV podcast — "Bringing Your Own Product to Market? Watch This First!", interview 7 Feb 2020**
Busch on manufacturing and fulfilment problems: he manufactures in Pakistan, was working on "version 2.0", and was switching fulfilment centres at the time. Notes bad Amazon reviews hurt, and copycats were a problem.
https://www.listennotes.com/bn/podcasts/inventrighttv/bringing-your-own-product-to-gGK_ThwpP9F/

**6. THINK Business LIVE with Jon Dwoskin — 16 Apr 2021**
"Being Resilient in every Situation." Jon Dwoskin talks with Howie Busch, "Founder & Dude-in-Chief of DudeRobe, about the power of launching a brand, its personality and scaling your business through the pandemic."
https://jondwoskin.com/2021/04/think-business-live-jon-dwoskin-talks-with-howie-busch/

**7. Boardroom — 15 Dec 2021**
"How DudeRobe's Menswear Got an Assist From the NBA's R&D Agency." The NBALAB deal (see Milestones). Busch quote: "Small businesses like my own are getting a boost in exchange for paying a higher royalty, but this is a great program for companies that do not have the financial means to get full licensing rights." Also names NFL running backs AJ Dillon (Green Bay Packers) and Alexander Mattison (Minnesota Vikings) as DudeRobe endorsers.
https://boardroom.tv/duderobe-apparel-nbalab/

**8. Looper — 23 May 2023**
"Whatever Happened To Duderobe After Shark Tank?" Post-show update: sales rose sharply after the episode; Busch told Sezzle in an interview that the company kept growing during the pandemic; NBA licensing deal; "estimated $2 million in gross revenue in 2021."
https://www.looper.com/1293440/whatever-happened-duderobe-shark-tank/

**9. Social Snowball, Instagram — 3 Feb 2025 (ST/REUNION24 event)**
Short video interview with Busch at the event. He repeats the origin story ("never a 'robe guy'… the idea came to him in the shower: combine a hoodie with a robe") and describes the features (regular/cuffed sleeves, permanently attached belt, hood).
https://www.instagram.com/reel/DFnuy9bvgqY/

**10. Yawnder — firsthand review, by Ben Trapskin, updated Jan 2026 (price checked 1 Nov 2026)**
Independent wear-test review (not a customer story): preferred the towel-like lining, oversized hood, secure pockets and attached belt over conventional loose robes; drawbacks were warmth, extra bulk and longer drying time. Notes the robe washed several times without noticeable fading or pilling. Price reference: $128 regular price, checked 1 Nov 2026.
https://yawnder.com/dude-robe-review/

**Brand-claimed media features (NOT independently verified per outlet):** the brand's Our Story page says: "Since Season 9 of ABC's Shark Tank, DudeRobe has been featured on Good Morning America, CNBC, Fox News, and in GQ, Men's Health, Esquire, Inked, and Newsweek." No individual article from those outlets was found in this research — treat as the brand's own claim, not as verified coverage.

## Customer stories (public only)

All quotes below are from the brand's own site (duderobe.com product pages and Our Story page) or the Shop app listing, marked "Verified buyer" where the source says so. No independent Trustpilot/BBB presence was found (see Gaps). No Reddit threads were found.

**Aggregate (duderobe.com, live Nov 2026):** the main robe product page shows **4.71 out of 5 from 2,440 reviews**. Kids robe: 4.78 (27 reviews). The brand states "worn by over 300,000 dudes" (brand claim, undated page) and that "almost half of our reviews are written by women who bought a DudeRobe as a gift for the men in their lives."

**Gift-giver stories (brand's Our Story page):**
- Tracy B., verified buyer: "My husband said he'd never want a robe… He absolutely loves it! He says it's like wearing a hoodie, light weight and comfortable. You've turned him into a morning robe guy!"
- Jennifer C., verified buyer: "My 2 sons loved their Dude Robes! They said it was their favorite gift!"
- Victoria H., verified buyer: "This was my husbands favorite gift in over 20 years. The fastened belt, pockets, quality, fit, soft/absorbent lining, cuffs and hood make the robe unique."
- Rolando S.: "I have never given a product of any kind a review. I don't care how good it is, I DON'T GIVE REVIEWS. But Dude, SERIOUSLY!!"
- Casey C.: "He's never owned a robe before but now he's obsessed. Last night I had to beg him not to wear it in the grocery store."
- Colleen M.: "Every single time he puts the pants on he yells 'I have reached a new level of comfort.'"
- Brandi H.: "I turned the AC down just to have a reason to wear the robe. Best gift ever."
- Erin S.: "DudeRobe clothing has become a household uniform."

**More (duderobe.com product pages, verified buyers):**
- "My boyfriend won't take it off!! He loves his robe and tells me how perfect of a gift it is. Everything from the hoodie, the sleeves when he cooks, down to the length. … He said he's never owned a robe before but he's now a dude robe man for life!"
- "I bought this for my husband for Christmas and he absolutely loves it. He says it's the perfect material, and all the details made it super worth it — the pockets, the hood, the sewn-on tie."
- "I gifted this robe to my boyfriend for Christmas and it was love at first feel! He immediately washed it and tested it straight out of the shower. It worked great at drying him off and the robe dried quickly as well. It's hard to get it off him!"
- JM G., verified buyer (kids robe): "He loved the DudeRobe. Super comfy and he doesn't want to take it off. Told me it was an excellent choice!"
- Teri S., verified buyer (kids robe): "Purchased for my grandson, I was impressed with the softness on the outside and the absorption on the inside. It's a great robe."

**UFC line (Shop app listing, customer, 27 Jan 2026):** "I bought 4 of them for my grown sons, the UFC robes, they absolutely love them!" — https://shop.app/products/9503608013086/ufc-duderobe-black

**Recurring themes in the public reviews:** bought as a gift (mostly by women for husbands/sons/boyfriends); "never a robe guy" converts; hoodie-not-bathrobe framing; attached belt, deep pockets, cuffs and absorbency praised most; Christmas/Father's Day gifting.

## Gaps / not found

- **No Reddit threads** about DudeRobe found (site:reddit.com search returned nothing).
- **No Trustpilot, BBB or Sitejabber presence** found for DudeRobe. A Nov 2023 review-aggregator page (fortyreviews.com) scored Trustpilot 0, BBB 0, Sitejabber 0 — i.e. no profiles exist there. All review material therefore comes from the brand's own site/Shop app.
- **No independent (non-brand) customer stories** beyond the Yawnder wear-test review. All customer quotes above are brand-hosted.
- **Indiegogo month conflicts:** Gazette Review says the Indiegogo campaign launched August 2017; Shark Tank Blog dates the $77,360 raise to November 2017. The amount is consistent; the month is not. Do not state a month without resolving this.
- **Revenue $2M is an estimate** from Shark Tank tracker sites, not an audited or company-reported figure. Do not present it as confirmed.
- **Media features claimed by the brand** (Good Morning America, CNBC, Fox News, GQ, Men's Health, Esquire, Inked, Newsweek) — no individual article from any of those outlets was found. Do not cite them as verified coverage.
- **UFC launch date:** announced 23 Aug 2025 on Instagram; no press release or dated launch announcement found.
- **University of Michigan robe launch date:** undated; product page exists.
- **No public information found** on: current team size, headquarters location, current manufacturing partners (beyond "manufacturing in Pakistan" in 2020), or any awards.
- **Founder's Under Armour involvement** is his own account as told on Shark Tank; not independently verified.

## Sources NOT used (and why)

- **modernmensrobe.com / en-theduderobe.com** — affiliate-style mirror/funnel sites with inflated, implausible claims ("99,162 reviews", "5,035 reviews", "6,900 verified five-star reviews", future-dated review stamps). Not reliable; nothing from them is used above.
- **sharktanksuccess.com "DUDE Products Update"** — claims DUDE Products "created the DudeRobe"; contradicts all primary sources. Treated as an error.
- **hustlerslibrary.com Dude Wipes case study** — contains factual errors (wrong Shark Tank season for Dude Wipes; "Brian Sherwood" for Brian Wilkin). Not used.
- **techtimes.com / accessnewswire.com "DudeRobe Reviews" pieces (Nov–Dec 2025)** — read as paid/affiliate content, not independent reporting. Not used for facts.
- **couponupto.com** — reposts brand-site reviews; the same quotes are cited above directly from duderobe.com instead.

**Brand:** DEFI Snacks (DEFI = "Delicious Energizing Fitness Indulgence")
**Website:** defi-snacks.com (current store); defisnacks.com (older domain, still live)
**Base:** Chatham, NJ
**Research date:** 2026-11-16
**Rule followed:** every item below comes from a published public source, cited with URL and date. Quotes are exact. Anything unverified is in Gaps, not filled in.

---

## 1. Origin / founder

**Founder:** Tatyana Jones — Ukrainian immigrant, former CPG executive, CrossFit enthusiast, MBA from NYU Stern.

**Corporate background (before founding):** Johnson & Johnson, Mars Wrigley (where she worked on Dove Chocolate), GSK Consumer, Bausch + Lomb.
- Source: Adventures Frugal Mom, "Top 10 Entrepreneurs Transforming Industries", published 2026-04-22 — "Before launching DEFI Snacks in November 2024, Tatyana built her impressive career working for big names like Johnson & Johnson, Mars Wrigley, GSK Consumer and Bausch + Lomb. This unique blend of corporate experience and education from NYU Stern School of Business helped Tatyana spot what was missing in the market."
- URL: https://adventuresfrugalmom.com/top-10-entrepreneurs-transforming-industries/
- Corroborated by Tapesearch ("Oh, My Health… There Is HOPE!" episode notes): "Tatyana has previously helped grow well-known brands such as Dove Chocolate and Mars Wrigley. An MBA graduate from NYU Stern…" — https://www.tapesearch.com/podcast/oh-my-health-there-is-hope/1477858454

**The origin story (brand's own account, About page):**
- "DEFI started in Tatyana's kitchen. Growing up Ukrainian, buckwheat was a staple — and when she moved to the US, she couldn't believe a superfood this good was practically unknown. (For the record: it's not a grain or a wheat. It's a flower seed — closer to a fruit.)"
- "The shelves were full of better-for-you snacks and full of indulgent ones — and nothing that was honestly both. So she started experimenting at home, then brought in a chef to develop many of the flavors you see today: real chocolate, sprouted buckwheat crunch, no compromises."
- "She didn't sell it at first. She brought batches to the gym and gave them away — and people kept coming back for more. Then a retailer placed a sizable order before ever tasting the product. That's when it was clear: DEFI wasn't just a snack. It was a brand."
- Source: DEFI Snacks About page — https://www.defi-snacks.com/pages/about (read 2026-11-16)

**Founder's own words (About page):**
- "As a fitness-loving foodie, I launched DEFI to revolutionize snacking. By choosing DEFI, you're not just enjoying a delicious snack – you're supporting a female-led brand that proudly donates a portion of its sales to women-run businesses that defy the odds, just like us."
- Source: https://www.defi-snacks.com/pages/about

**Why buckwheat (founder quote, press release):**
- "Most people assume buckwheat is a wheat or some type of a grain," says Tatyana. "In reality, it's neither. Buckwheat is a naturally gluten-free flower seed, and nutritionally outperforms many of today's trendy ingredients. It's great for your gut, is loaded with fiber, protein, vitamins and antioxidants… and the list goes on."
- Source: CPG Media / BevNET newswire, 2026-01-13 — https://www.cpgmedia.com/newswire/2026/01/13/redefining-betterforyou-snacking-defi-snacks-combines-superfood-innovation-with-timereleased-fuel

**How the product was built:**
- After moving to the US and spotting the gap, "Tatyana partnered with a trusted scientist to explore white-space opportunities for a buckwheat-based product. After much experimentation and category analysis, she identified a clear gap in the market: snacks that are truly indulgent, yet go beyond empty calories with nutrient density and function."
- "Shortly after, Tatyana partnered with Chef Jean-François Bonnet, known for helping formulate many of the original Hu Chocolate flavors before the brand was sold to snacking giant, Mondelez."
- Source: CPG Media newswire, 2026-01-13 (same URL as above)
- Corroborated by Expo West 2026 exhibitor listing: "As a passionate Ukrainian immigrant with a love for fitness and wholesome food, I founded DEFI Snacks to share my heritage and vision with the world. Growing up in Ukraine, I cherished buckwheat — a nutrient-rich, gluten-free staple… I dreamed of creating a snack that married my cultural roots with my active lifestyle as a dedicated CrossFitter." — https://attend.expowest.com/event/natural-products-expo-west-2026/exhibitor/RXhoaWJpdG9yXzIzNTg5NDg=

**Launch:** November 2024 (product launch; see Milestones).
- Source: Adventures Frugal Mom, 2026-04-22 (same URL as above)

**Mission / giving (wording varies by source — keep source wording):**
- About page: "With every bag sold, we donate 1% of sales to women-owned businesses. Less than 2% of venture funding goes to female founders. We're here to change that. DEFI is a proud partner of the Enthuse Foundation, a nonprofit dedicated to empowering women entrepreneurs to grow from new to next."
- Press release (2026-01-13): "As a female-founded company, DEFI donates 1% of its profitable sales to women-owned startups that defy the odds."
- Source: https://www.defi-snacks.com/pages/about and https://www.cpgmedia.com/newswire/2026/01/13/redefining-betterforyou-snacking-defi-snacks-combines-superfood-innovation-with-timereleased-fuel

**Product (for context, from the Jan 2026 press release):** four crispy chocolate bites — Dark Chocolate Himalayan Salt, Dark Chocolate, Milk Chocolate, Milk Chocolate Peanut Butter Crunch (new). 25–26g protein per bag. Built on sprouted organic buckwheat + whey protein crisps (fast energy) + European-grade casein (slow digestion, longer fullness). No sugar substitutes.
- Source: CPG Media newswire, 2026-01-13 (same URL as above)

### Themes across real customer voices (summarised from the above, not invented)
- "Tastes like real chocolate, not a protein bar" — the most repeated theme.
- Two pieces are enough to feel satisfied — portion control as a feature.

- Recurring complaints: bag size vs $15 price; melting/clusters stuck together in transit; buckwheat taste takes getting used to.

## 5. Gaps / not found

Do not fill these with invented material. Each needs the brand/owner to supply it, or a future verified source.

1. **Exact founding date.** Only the product launch (November 2024) is published. Company formation date, and when Tatyana left corporate, are not published.
2. **Shelfies win vs finalist.** Startup CPG's own page confirms DEFI as a 2025 Shelfie *finalist* (Aug 2025). The brand's Jan 2026 release claims a "Shelfies Award Winner". No winners list was found to confirm a win. Treat as finalist until confirmed.
3. **RangeMe #3 ranking, Food & Beverage Magazine Editor's Top Pick, Sports Illustrated quote.** All appear only in the brand's own materials (press release / homepage). No independent article found for any of the three.
4. **Mintel award year wording.** CPG Latest (Nov 2026) and the brand's store say "2026 Mintel Most Innovative Product award" winner. The brand's Facebook unboxing video (Jul 2026) describes the physical box as the "2025 Mintel Most Innovative Award". Minor discrepancy — likely the award-cycle year vs the announcement year. Do not overstate; cite as "2026 Mintel Most Innovative Product award (reported Nov 2026)".
5. **Good Morning America segment.** Verified only via the brand's own Instagram reel and its press release. No ABC/GMA page or clip link found. Do not cite a GMA URL.
6. **Funding.** Only the $1.5M target (announced Jan 2026). No closed round, no investor names, no valuation published. The Enthuse prize ($250K+ cash and in-kind; $15K cash check) is the only confirmed funding-type inflow.
7. **Revenue / sales figures.** None published. The Enthuse reel mentions a "$100K to $250K in projected revenue in one year" *competition bracket* — that is a bracket, not actual revenue. Do not use it as a sales figure.
8. **No customer case studies or long-form interviews.** What exists: short store/TikTok reviews, creator reels, and podcast interviews with the founder. No published in-depth customer story (e.g. a named customer transformation story) was found.
9. **No team, manufacturing, or HQ detail beyond Chatham, NJ.** Headcount, co-packer/manufacturer, and office details are not published.
10. **No Reddit threads or forum discussion found** for DEFI Snacks in this pass (searched reviews/testimonials generally; Reddit returned nothing). Do not claim Reddit sentiment either way.
11. **RangeMe article full text not retrievable.** Title, author (Joe Tarnowski) and date (2026-07-14) confirmed via RangeMe's own index pages; the article page returned the blog index when fetched. Quotes from it are therefore NOT included above.
12. **The "16 permanent locations and 100 NYC retailer trials" figure** comes from a single third-party listicle (Adventures Frugal Mom, Apr 2026, describing the first ~3 months). Not corroborated elsewhere. Use with that attribution.
13. **Founder's full name spelling.** "Tatyana Jones" is consistent across the brand, press and LinkedIn. One podcast transcript index spells it "Tatiana" — that is a transcription error, not an alternate spelling.
